newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Pasminco sets US$600 mln debt facility.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Pasminco sets US$600 mln debt facility.

text.p: Base metals miner Pasminco Ltd said on Thursday it had appointed arrangers for a US$600 million debt facility to help fund the acquisition of Century Zinc Ltd from Rio Tinto Ltd and develop the Century mine in Queensland.
Citibank, Commonwealth Bank of Australia and Deutsche Bank were appointed joint arrangers of the debt facility.

Pasminco announced in April that it had appointed J.B. Were & Sons and SBC Warburg Australia Ltd as joint underwriters for the equity raising, which is expected to take place after Pasminco's acquisiton of Century Zinc is completed.

"Pasminco has now completed arrangements for the Century debt and equity funding package and the procedures required to finalise the acquisition are being pursued as quickly as possible," Pasminco executive general manager, finance, Bronwyn Constance said in a statement.

Pasminco said that to expedite development of Century mine, Century Zinc has started remobilisation of the engineering team and would undertake preliminary site infrastructure projects. The cost of development of the mine is estimated at A$1 billion.

In January, Pasminco said it would buy the Century mine and the nearby Dugald River zinc projects for A$345 million from global miner Rio Tinto, formerly CRA-RTZ, conditional on the Queensland state government issuing mining leases which depended on Aboriginal groups resolving an impasse over land title.
In May, Century Zinc secured an agreement with indigenous communities and the Queensland government.
Pasminco has said it would fund the A$345 million purchase price from existing loan facilities.
Pasminco bought the mine because it needs Century's low-iron zinc concentrates to feed its Budel smelter in the Netherlands.
The company has said the low-iron concentrates would ensure the smelter complied with a requirement that it cease generating hazardous zinc residue called jarosite.
The Century mine is forecast to produce annually 780,000 tonnes of zinc concentrates. If development work starts in the next few months, Pasminco sees production from as early as 1999.
